briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Chains Go Bigger, Federal Cannabis Reform Grinds Forward
briefs.top: Michigan's JARS Cannabis just bought its way to becoming Arizona's largest dispensary chain even as the state's 24% wholesale tax keeps underperforming projections, and a governor's-race endorsement puts repeal squarely on the table. Nationally, Compass Pathways landed an FDA priority voucher that could put a psilocybin depression drug on the market by 2027, while Curaleaf's billion-dollar bid for Aurora Cannabis and fresh MSO credit lines show capital is flowing again ahead of a still-pending DEA rescheduling call.

local.text: JARS Cannabis becomes Arizona's biggest chain — The Michigan-based operator is acquiring Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa dispensaries, a deal that will make JARS the largest dispensary chain in Arizona.

Wyld's Grön Pearls gummies hit Michigan shelves — The Portland-based edibles brand's bestselling Pearls gummies launched in Michigan as part of a four-state rollout, already confirmed at Pure Options, High Profile and Lume.

Muskegon dispensary-restaurant hybrid targets fall debut — Fields Cannary is building a full-service restaurant alongside its retail cannabis dispensary, pushing the format further than most Michigan stores have gone.

Cannabis industry rallies behind tax-repeal candidate — MiCIA endorsed GOP gubernatorial nominee John James, who has pledged to repeal the 24% wholesale tax he says has "fallen far short of revenue projections."

Wholesale tax collections still trailing far behind forecast — The 24% levy generated roughly $37 million in Q2 and $34 million in Q1, against an initial estimate of $105 million per quarter, bolstering operators' case for reform.

national.text: Compass Pathways scores FDA priority voucher for psilocybin — The agency granted a rolling NDA review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for COMP360, its psilocybin treatment for treatment-resistant depression.
Compass eyes first-half 2027 psilocybin launch — Executives said the NDA submission should complete in Q4 with a potential U.S. launch in the first half of 2027 as the FDA's rolling review advances.

Curaleaf pursues $1.5B+ cross-border Aurora Cannabis deal — Curaleaf's takeover bid, offering a 45% premium, signals major U.S. multistate operators are now confident enough in the regulatory backdrop to chase Canadian targets.
Cresco Labs lands $50M credit line ahead of Schedule III — Needham Bank's financing gives Cresco a non-dilutive tool to fund acquisitions and positions it for a future uplisting to a senior exchange.

DEA's broader rescheduling call still pending, but momentum builds — In its own post-hearing brief the DEA argued marijuana no longer meets Schedule I criteria, even as a state regulator says the agency is offering no guidance on next steps.
